## Fast fixes

| Symptom | Why / exact next step |
|---|---|
| Unknown capability / wrong kind | Check the capability table and change ether.kind or remove the unsupported capability; artwork/ratings are reserved |
| Cannot import module in hosted runtime | Bundle local SDK imports into the entry artifact; no npm resolution in QuickJS |
| `ether` / process / fs unavailable | Use hosted host services, or choose a remote sidecar for OS APIs |
| Permission denied | Declare the exact permission/hostname, reinstall, then have the owner grant it; never retry around revocation |
| Missing settings/strings file | Include the $ref/i18n path inside the package; run check again |
| Empty content library | Complete required setup, enable the plugin, check sync cursors and its mediaKind descriptors |
| Conformance route failed | Read rule + field + route; implement its exact response shape from Reference → Capabilities, then rerun check |
| Dev 401/403 | Set ETHER_TOKEN to the local server's admin token and review its requested grants |
| Dev connection refused | Start your local server and pass its actual --server URL/port |
| Dev install conflicts | Check existing plugin ID/version; do not change identity on every save |
| Labels rejected | Sentence case, length limits, no banned words/punctuation; translate every referenced key |

Before reporting success: review the diff, compile the chosen language, run
conformance, package, and check the visible result on your own development server.
Never claim offline conformance proves playback on a real client. New host
services belong in the generated reference source list and this service map;
regenerate the reference instead of duplicating contracts in prose.

## Slow resolution and remote verification

Kind `/resolve` and `/match` handlers may return `{pending:true,retryInMs:1000}`.
Ether retries after 250–5000 ms (clamped), for at most 25 seconds per Play;
each invocation is capped at 12 seconds for `/resolve` and five seconds for
`/match`. Pending does not damage health.
If a call is still `pending` after the 25-second wait budget, Ether answers
`503` with `code: "preparing"` and `Retry-After` (from `retryInMs`, or `5` s by
default) on `kind-media`, Vela, Jellyfin and Plex API routes without caching a
negative resolution; only a real empty `sources: []` / `404` answer becomes `409`
`no_source`. For slow searches, also return `job:"/ether/job/prepare"`. Ether
deduplicates running jobs per plugin, kind, item, `partIndex`, and `source`, passes the
original request body, and uses the existing promoted job deadline and
continuation protocol. A completed
job wakes the resolver before the retry timer. Persist results in KV; never do
work ahead of an actual request. Owner/scheduled jobs (up to 2) and playback
resolver jobs (up to 4) have separate limits per plugin; if all four resolver
slots are busy, Ether returns `503` with `code: "jobs_busy"` and `Retry-After`.

`ether.http.fetch({url,timeoutMs:1200})` and
`ether.http.fetchToCache({url,libraryKey,name,timeoutMs:1200,resume:true})` bound a slow
remote request (including streaming into cache) by the remaining call deadline.
`http.fetchToCache` defaults to 10 minutes (also the ceiling on viewer and
interactive request paths); inside a job (`/ether/job/*`), schedule, or
background context (`kind` / Live TV sync, `/ether/event`), `timeoutMs` may
extend up to the calling job's remaining deadline. Pass `resume: true` to
continue an incomplete partial blob with `Range: bytes=<cached>-` when the
server supports ranges and strong `ETag` or `Last-Modified` validators still
match (restarting cleanly from byte 0 if they do not or the server returns
`200`/`416`); partial bytes count against the library cache quota and disk
safety floor and only become a readable cache blob once complete.
In jobs, schedules, and background calls, set `connections` (1–6, default 1)
to request parallel ranges, sharing the host's limit of 6 per origin. The
server must advertise byte ranges, a known length, and a strong validator.
Ranges served from a different URL need the same strong ETag and total
length as the probe. Use `resume: true` to continue each range's saved progress.
Hosted code can catch `e.code === "timeout"`. Remote SDK fetches use their local
request context/timeout.

`ether.http.fetchMany(requests, {concurrency?})` runs up to 64 outbound HTTP
requests concurrently on the host while the hosted guest waits synchronously,
overlapping independent provider or candidate-detail fetches instead of summing
their latencies. Per-call concurrency defaults to and clamps at 8 (fixed host
cap, no owner setting), per-origin politeness limits cap concurrent fetches to
6 per origin across Ether (with origin-interleaved scheduling so one saturated
host does not head-of-line block others), total buffered response bodies across
the batch are bounded at 10 MiB (`MaxFetchManyBytes`), and governance charges
100 units per request (identical to individual `http.fetch` calls). Answers
return in input order: each item has either `{status, headers, body, bodyBase64?}`
(including non-2xx HTTP status codes) or `{error: {code, message}}` on per-item
timeout, permission, redirect, size, or transport failure. Canceling the parent
request or exceeding its deadline aborts all in-flight batch fetches promptly
without consuming extra WASM pool lanes.

Indexer search results give you `nzbRef` for Usenet and `torrentRef` when a
torrent needs a descriptor lookup. The deprecated link fields mirror these
references with an `ether-nzb:` or `ether-torrent:` prefix. Call
`ether.sources.resolve({kind: "nzb_request", nzbRef})` for the file list and
permanent vault reference. Use that reference in a release source's
`release.nzbRef`, and use `release_files` for files inside archives.
Use this service for indexer search and NZB access from hosted, HTTP and
tunnel plugins. Ether blocks its own plugin HTTP requests to configured indexer
hosts. The indexer API URL and credentials stay in Ether's indexer settings.
Plugin settings and secrets hold only that plugin's configuration. Do not ask
owners to copy their indexer URLs or API keys into plugin settings. Source
results carry opaque download references and trackerless magnets.

An HTTP or tunnel sidecar runs under its own OS or container permissions.
Ether controls what it sends to that process and requests Ether makes on its
behalf. To enforce the same egress restriction on a sidecar's own traffic,
restrict its outbound connections through its container network policy or
host firewall.

Across all host HTTP paths (`http.fetch`, `http.fetchMany`, `http.fetchToCache`, `http.hash`, and
playable `range`/`download`/`direct`/`container` sources), redirects recheck
live network permissions on every hop and keep credentials/caller headers only
on the same origin, a strict same-site subdomain (verified via the Public Suffix
List with no port change or HTTPS→HTTP downgrade), or an explicit
`keepHeadersOnRedirect: ["cdn.example.net", "*.storage.example.org"]` host
pattern within granted network permissions (never `*`, never a public suffix,
never across HTTPS→HTTP downgrades, and sticky once any hop leaves trusted hosts).

`ether.http.hash({url,algo:"sha256",expectSize:12345,headers:{Cookie:"{secret:session}"},keepHeadersOnRedirect:["*.storage.example.org"]})` returns either
`{pending:true,retryInMs:1000}` or `{size,sha256,sha1,md5}`. `expectSize`,
`headers`, and `keepHeadersOnRedirect` are optional; algorithms are `sha256`, `sha1`, `md5`. Hashing streams
on the host, without a blob or guest bytes, through the same network permissions
and safe fetch rules as fetch. Optional `headers` expand `{secret:<name>}`
placeholders using the plugin's `permissions.secrets` grant (including derived
secrets stored via `secret.set`), reject hop-by-hop/framing headers (`Connection`,
`Host`, `Content-Length`, `Range`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Proxy-*`, etc.), follow
the same redirect credential policy (stripped on untrusted redirects), are never logged, and are
not part of the hash cache key. It starts only when called. One worker per plugin and
two globally run below playback priority and yield during playback contention.
Disable/uninstall cancels work. Limits: 64 GiB per file, 50 GiB per plugin per
UTC day (including unsuccessful reads), 12 hours per task. The daily cap logs
at Info. Cached digests share one read across algorithms, are private to the
plugin and URL, and include response validators and size. A hit returns
immediately for five minutes; later calls return pending while the host
conditionally revalidates ETag/Last-Modified or streams a new digest. Up to
2048 entries are kept per plugin. Failed tasks may be retried after 30 seconds.
Remote Go uses `RemoteHostClient.Hash`; TypeScript/Python use `http.hash`.

```js
// The manifest must declare the upstream in permissions.network.
function resolve(req) {
  const result = ether.http.hash({url:req.item.hints.url, algo:"sha256"});
  if (result.pending) return {status:200, body:result};
  if (result.sha256 !== req.item.hints.sha256)
    return {status:404, body:{sources:[]}};
  return {status:200, body:{sources:[{pattern:"http",url:req.item.hints.url}]}};
}
// A slow search instead returns pending with job:"/ether/job/prepare";
// that handler writes a KV result and returns {done:true}, or checkpoints with
// {continueInMs:1000,continuation:{cursor:"next"}}. Resolve reads that KV result.
```

## Frontend adapter downloads

Authenticated frontend adapter requests carry `X-Ether-Origin`
(`scheme://host[:port][/prefix]`, derived from trusted proxies only with any
inbound client `X-Ether-Origin` stripped) alongside `X-Ether-Viewer`.

Hosted adapters can return a redirect to a host-minted item stream URL, a
specific zero-based part when an item declares `hints.parts`, a specific
resolver `PlayableSource.id`, or an absolute URL (`{ absolute: true }`) for
native clients (such as Kodi or Subsonic apps) that play URLs verbatim:

```js
// Whole item (concatenated sequence for multi-part items):
return {status:302, headers:{Location:ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef).url}};
// Single part (resolves with KindResolveRequest.partIndex = partIndex):
return {status:302, headers:{Location:ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef, partIndex).url}};
// Specific resolver source (and optional partIndex) with no failover:
return {status:302, headers:{Location:ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef, {partIndex, source: "epub"}).url}};
// Absolute URL for protocol documents (falls back to the adapter's first published address):
const playUrl = ether.frontend.streamURL(itemRef, {absolute: true}).url;
```

In the SDKs, call `streamUrl(ctx, itemRef, partIndexOrOpts?)` (TypeScript),
`ctx.StreamURLWithOptions(itemRef, StreamURLOptions{PartIndex, Source, Fallback, Absolute, Wait})` or
`ctx.StreamPartURL(itemRef, partIndex)` (Go), or
`ctx.stream_url(item_ref, part_index=..., source=..., fallback=True, absolute=...)` (Python); an unpinned
item ticket also accepts `/ether/v1/kind-media/{ticket}?part=N`. Default stream
URLs remain root-relative; `{ absolute: true }` prepends the request's
`X-Ether-Origin` (falling back to the adapter's first published address in
`frontends["plugin:<id>:<adapter>"].publishedAddresses`, preserving any path
prefix, when the request has none). Multi-file
items declare `hints.parts: [{name, mime?, size?, durationSec?}, ...]` (or a
declared `parts` field) so Ether resolves and caches each part with its
zero-based `KindResolveRequest.partIndex`; playable items with no declared parts
reject any `partIndex` with `404 item_not_found`. When `source` is set on the
ticket grant, Ether passes `KindResolveRequest.source` to `/resolve` and opens
only the matching `PlayableSource.id` without failing over to other sources (a
plugin that ignores `source` still works because Ether selects the matching id
or returns `409 no_source` if absent). Add `fallback: true` to treat the source as a preference. If it is missing or fails to open, Ether tries the remaining sources for the same part in their usual order.

For an adapter download route, pass `{wait: {maxSeconds: 1200}}` to hold the
media response while the plugin prepares the file. In Go, use
`Wait: &etherplugin.StreamWaitPolicy{MaxSeconds: 1200}`. Use a positive integer.
Ether caps the wait at 1800 seconds and allows up to four held requests per
plugin and 32 per server. Over that limit, the request uses the ordinary media
open and can return 503 with `Retry-After` while preparation continues.
Omit `wait` on player routes to keep their 18-second default. Choose a wait below
the client's and reverse proxy's response-header timeouts so Ether can send its
own retry response. Disconnects release the held request while the job continues.

Only root-relative local redirect URLs are forwarded. External URLs, authority
changes, control characters, backslashes and known account credential query
parameters are refused. Use the scoped host media ticket, never a login token.

For a cached file or verified archive member, return a blob descriptor instead
of `body` (status 200). The bytes never pass through guest memory:

```js
return {status:200, blob:{
  libraryKey:"pk-my-plugin-firmware", ref:cachedBlobRef, memberIndex:member.index
}};
```

Use the canonical library key returned for your declared media kind. Omit
`memberIndex` to serve the whole blob. The host rechecks enabled state, frontend
capability, ownership, current viewer visibility and the adapter's library list
on every request. It opens only that library's cache namespace and applies the
existing archive safety and runtime limits. The plugin must verify expected
hashes before selecting a cached member; delivery does not assert hash validity.
When trusted metadata provides SHA-1 or MD5 rather than CRC32, call
`ether.archive.extract(cachedBlobRef, member.index)` to stream the member into the
library cache and verify `sha1`/`md5` before serving `{libraryKey, ref: extracted.ref}`.

GET and HEAD are supported. A single GET byte range receives 206; malformed,
multiple or unsatisfiable ranges receive 416. HEAD ignores Range. Downloads use
`application/octet-stream`, a fixed safe attachment filename, no-store and
nosniff; plugin response headers do not override these. Archive range offsets
may require bounded decompression from the start, so do not use this path for
unbounded repeated seeks. Existing JSON `body` responses are unchanged. Remote
HTTP plugins should stream bytes through their existing HTTP response instead;
this descriptor is for the hosted JSON response envelope.

## Recipe: Frontend adapter respecting library Rules

`kinds.items` reads a plugin's raw kind items without evaluating the library's
Rules or viewer visibility. A `frontend_adapter` serving its own protocol
(OPDS, Subsonic, WebDAV, custom clients) must filter through Ether's policy so
items hidden by Rules, hidden libraries, viewer library grants, or viewer
content-safety restrictions never leak to the adapter's clients.

Ether exposes two viewer-scoped host calls that run the exact same
`LibraryPolicy` + `libraryfilter` + viewer-safety checks as the console and
built-in protocol projectors:

- `kinds.browse(kind, query)` — browse or search a kind page with policy already
  applied for the requesting viewer (`{parentId?, level?, cursor?, limit?, sort?, desc?, facets?, allFacets?, excludeFacets?, anyGroups?, empty?, query?, excludeQuery?, total?}`).
  `anyGroups` entries accept `{field, values}` or cross-field `{any: [{field, values}, ...]}` (values across every alternative count toward the 256-value bound); `empty` maps field names (declared fields or item columns like `released`, `year`, `rating`, `summary`, `recording`) to `true` (missing) or `false` (present) without counting toward value bounds (unknown fields are rejected); `excludeQuery` drops items matching the same text search as `query`.
  `total` defaults to `"cheap"` (returns `total` only when O(1) from tallies/cache/single page, omitting it otherwise); pass `"none"` to skip totals or `"exact"` when a caller needs an exact filtered count.
  Prefer this when your adapter lists or searches pages directly from Ether's library.
- `kinds.visible(kind, ids)` — check a batch of up to **500** external IDs and
  return only the IDs visible to the requesting viewer, preserving caller order
  and dropping unknown or hidden IDs. Use this when your adapter builds a custom
  list or keeps its own index and needs to prune hidden items before returning them.

- `kinds.get(kind, ids)` — the stored items (up to **500**) the viewer may see, in
  request order (hosted JS).
- Viewer state for your own items, stored in Ether's shared favourites, watch
  state and playlists (a like here is a like in every Ether app), hosted JS:
  `kinds.state`, `kinds.favorite`, `kinds.played`, `kinds.rate`,
  `kinds.favorites`, `kinds.playlists`, `kinds.playlist`, `kinds.playlistCreate`,
  `kinds.playlistUpdate`, `kinds.playlistDelete`. See docs/plugin-kinds.md › Host services.
- `kinds.expand(kind, id)` and `kinds.search(kind, query, {limit?})` (hosted JS) ask
  Ether to open a container or search the way an Ether app does, so a pull-synced
  kind gets its children or live-search finds stored without the adapter pushing
  anything; then read them with `kinds.browse`. `expand` answers `{pending}`,
  `search` answers `{found}`.
- Adapter auth `query_credentials` (Subsonic `u` + `p`/`t`+`s`) authenticates
  Ether-issued per-viewer app logins; failed requests are relayed to
  `/ether/v1/frontend/{key}/.unauthenticated/…` without a viewer so you can answer
  your protocol's own error. Answer `{media: {itemRef}}` or `{art: {itemRef, role}}`
  to have Ether serve an item's bytes (with ranges) or artwork at the adapter URL.

**Security guard:** Only viewer-authenticated frontend adapter requests
(`/ether/v1/frontend/*` on a plugin with `frontend_adapter`) may call
`kinds.visible`, `kinds.browse`, `kinds.expand`, `kinds.search` or the viewer-state calls above. Any other route (catalogue browse, jobs,
views, actions, unauthenticated requests) receives a permission error. The
viewer identity always comes from Ether's authenticated request context (and the
host-minted, request-scoped `X-Ether-Viewer-Token` header on remote plugin
callbacks) — never from guest-supplied parameters.

Hosted QuickJS (`plugin.js`):

```js
// Browse/search with Rules and viewer policy already applied:
const page = ether.kinds.browse("comic", { level: "series", limit: 50, query: q });

// Or filter your own candidate IDs in chunks of at most 500:
const allowedIds = ether.kinds.visible("comic", candidateIds.slice(0, 500));
const allowed = new Set(allowedIds);
const visible = candidates.filter((it) => allowed.has(it.id));
```

TypeScript SDK (`@ether/plugin-sdk`, hosted or sidecar):

```ts
import { kindsBrowse, kindsVisible } from "@ether/plugin-sdk";

app.onFrontend("opds", {
  async handle(method, path, _headers, _body, ctx) {
    if (!ctx) return { status: 500, body: "" };
    const page = await kindsBrowse(ctx, "comic", { limit: 50 });
    const visibleIds = await kindsVisible(ctx, "comic", page.items.map((it) => it.id));
    return { status: 200, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(visibleIds) };
  },
});
```

Go SDK (`sdk/go`):

```go
func (a *adapter) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    pctx, ok := etherplugin.FrontendContext(r.Context())
    if !ok {
        http.Error(w, "missing context", http.StatusForbidden)
        return
    }
    page, err := pctx.KindBrowse("comic", etherplugin.KindBrowseQuery{Limit: 50})
    if err != nil {
        http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusForbidden)
        return
    }
    visibleIDs, err := pctx.KindVisible("comic", candidateIDs) // <= 500 IDs per call
    _ = page
    _ = visibleIDs
}
```

Python SDK (`sdk/python`):

```python
class Adapter:
    def handle(self, method, path, headers, body, ctx):
        page = ctx.kinds_browse("comic", {"limit": 50})
        visible_ids = ctx.kinds_visible("comic", candidate_ids[:500])
        return 200, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, json.dumps({"ids": visible_ids, "count": len(page["items"])})
```


## Report route failures to the owner

Return a non-2xx status and a JSON body in this shape:

```json
{"error":{"code":"rate_limited","message":"The catalogue service is rate limiting requests","retryAfterSeconds":300}}
```

Use one credential-free, owner-facing sentence. Name the upstream service where
helpful. Supported codes are `auth` (upstream rejected credentials or access),
`rate_limited`, `upstream_unavailable`, `not_found` and `invalid_settings`.
Report upstream 401/403 as `auth` even if your route sends a 502. Send an optional
positive integer `retryAfterSeconds` or an HTTP `Retry-After` header for a
temporary failure. Use 501 for an unimplemented optional catalogue changes feed.

In TypeScript, throw `new PluginHttpError(429, "rate_limited", message, 300)`.
In Python, raise `PluginHttpError(429, "rate_limited", message, retry_after_seconds=300)`.
In Go, return `&etherplugin.RouteError{Status: 429, Code: "rate_limited", Message: message, RetryAfterSeconds: 300}`.

# Ether catalogue template

Ether reads the official signed plugin marketplace (`https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`, published at `https://braedonsaunders.github.io/ether-plugins/index.json`) by default. To submit a plugin to the official marketplace, upload `<id>-<version>.etherpkg` to a GitHub release, run `ether plugin publish --url <release-asset-url> <dir>` to generate `plugins/<id>.yaml`, and open a pull request against `https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`. Use this template only when operating your own catalogue and setting `plugins.indexUrl` and `plugins.publicKey` together in Ether's configuration.

Set the repository variable `ETHER_REF` to an immutable Ether release tag or commit that includes `ether plugin check` and `ether-release-sign index -check`. The workflow installs both tools from that ref. Set the `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PRIVATE_KEY` and `ETHER_CATALOGUE_PUBLIC_KEY` repository secrets to the base64 Ed25519 signing key and corresponding public key. Keep the private key secret. Pull requests validate without access to signing secrets; pushes to `main` sign and upload `index.json` and `index.json.sig` as a workflow artifact. Publish both files together at the `plugins.indexUrl` configured in Ether.

Add one reviewed YAML file per plugin under `plugins/`; `examples/` contains an illustrative file with placeholder URLs and checksums. Each version must reference a publicly downloadable `.etherpkg` and its SHA-256 digest. CI downloads every non-revoked version, verifies the digest and identity, and runs `ether plugin check` on its unpacked files. The command runs the conformance kit, including copy lint. The index compiler also validates catalogue copy. A revoked entry requires a reason; it is retained in the signed index and its packages are not executed by CI.

Review permissions for each version. A version may override the entry-level permissions using its own `permissions` field. Ether verifies that the package does not request more than the reviewed permissions before marking it verified. Never use the sample values as a real catalogue entry.

# Anime Tosho

One-click anime indexer plugin for Ether backed by [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net).

## What it does

The original Anime Tosho (`animetosho.org`) stopped indexing new releases in May 2026. [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net) is a community-funded successor that mirrors anime torrents from Nyaa.si, TokyoTosho, and nekoBT (2017 to present) and exposes open Torznab and Newznab feeds at `https://feed.animetosho.net` with no API key and no account required.

Installing this plugin adds Anime Tosho as an indexer source in Ether with nothing to paste:

- **Torrents and Usenet NZB mirrors:** returns torrent info hashes with public trackers from Torznab, Usenet NZB links from Newznab, or both at once.
- **Anime-aware search:** supports AniDB (`aid`), MyAnimeList (`malid`), Kitsu (`kitsuid`), TMDB (`tmdbid`), TVDB (`tvdbid`), and IMDb (`imdbid`) lookups, absolute episode numbering (such as long-running series like One Piece), and whole-season packs.
- **No API key:** Anime Tosho NEW's Torznab and Newznab feeds are open since v1.3.1, so connection tests and searches work immediately after installation.

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Release types** (`releaseTypes`) | `Torrents and NZBs` | Choose whether searches return public torrents, Usenet NZB mirrors, or both. NZB downloads require a Usenet provider configured in Ether. |
| **Category filter** (`category`) | `All categories` | Optional Torznab/Newznab category filter (`5070` for Anime, `2020` for Movies) passed to Anime Tosho NEW. |

## Public torrents notice

Torrents mirrored on Anime Tosho NEW come from public anime trackers such as Nyaa.si and nekoBT. They are **public torrents**, so Ether's private-torrent ratio and H&R rules do not apply to releases from this plugin.

## Credits and polite usage

All feed data, torrent metadata, and Usenet NZB mirrors are provided by [Anime Tosho NEW](https://animetosho.net), a free community-funded project, with ID mappings from AnimeAPI and the Anime Offline Database (ODbL-1.0).

This plugin identifies itself honestly with Ether's User-Agent (`Ether/0.3 (+https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether)`), makes a single bounded feed request per search (`limit=75`), declares conservative indexer rate limits (`120` searches/hour, `1000` searches/day), and propagates upstream `429` / `Retry-After` responses so Ether backs off automatically.

## Development

```sh
go run ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho/build
```

Run the plugin conformance check, fixture tests, and Go integration suite:

```sh
ether plugin check ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho
ether plugin test ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho
go test ./sdk/examples/anime-tosho/...
```

# English dubbed anime

First-party Ether plugin that exposes anime series and films with an English dub as ready-made list sources for Home rows, smart collections, and library rules.

## What it provides

- **Anime with an English dub (`dubbed`)** — TV series and films confirmed to have an English dub in the community MAL-Dubs dataset.
- **Dub in progress (`incomplete`)** — TV series and films whose English dub is still being released.
- **Status page** — Displays cached mapped series, movie, and in-progress counts with a manual cache refresh action.

## How it works

The plugin fetches both upstream datasets at runtime and does not bundle any copy of the data:

1. **Dub status list:** [MAL-Dubs](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs) (`data/dubInfo.json`, ~5,700 MyAnimeList IDs across `dubbed` and `incomplete`).
2. **ID mapping:** [Fribb/anime-lists](https://github.com/Fribb/anime-lists) (`anime-list-mini.json`), used at runtime to map MyAnimeList IDs to TMDB IDs (with IMDb and TVDB fallbacks where a TMDB ID is absent) because Ether's list source resolver matches canonical IMDb, TMDB, and TVDB identities.

Both files are cached in plugin KV storage in compacted form and refreshed daily via a scheduled job (`/ether/job/refresh`) using conditional HTTP requests (`ETag` / `If-None-Match` and `Last-Modified` / `If-Modified-Since`). If an upstream refresh fails transiently after the cache is populated, the plugin serves the previously cached index.

## Settings

| Setting | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Include incomplete dubs (`includeIncomplete`) | Boolean | `false` | Merges entries from the `incomplete` array into the main **Anime with an English dub** list (deduplicated by title). |
| Type filter (`typeFilter`) | Select (`both`, `series`, `movies`) | `both` | Restricts catalog responses to anime series, anime movies, or both. |

## Permissions

- **Network (`raw.githubusercontent.com`)** — Used only to fetch `MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs` (`data/dubInfo.json`) and `Fribb/anime-lists` (`anime-list-mini.json`).

## Credits and licenses

- Plugin source code: MIT License.
- Dub list data: [MAL-Dubs](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs), licensed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)](https://github.com/MAL-Dubs/MAL-Dubs/blob/main/LICENSE). No copy of the MAL-Dubs data is bundled with this plugin; it is fetched directly at runtime by each server.
- Anime ID mapping: [Fribb/anime-lists](https://github.com/Fribb/anime-lists).

## Limits

- **Community-maintained data:** Dub coverage and completeness depend on volunteer updates to MAL-Dubs; newly announced simuldubs or recent releases may lag behind broadcast dates.
- **MAL-to-TMDB mapping gaps:** Not every MyAnimeList entry (especially OVAs, specials, and newer titles) has a TMDB, TVDB, or IMDb mapping in `Fribb/anime-lists`. Unmapped entries cannot be matched to Ether's canonical catalogue and are omitted.
- **Season collapsing:** MyAnimeList assigns separate IDs per season or cour, while TMDB groups seasons under one show. Duplicate TMDB show IDs are collapsed into a single show entry, so a show appears once if at least one of its seasons is listed as dubbed.
- **Collection item limit:** Ether bounds each collection or Home row list source read to at most 2,000 items per refresh. The confirmed dubbed series list currently exceeds 2,000 TMDB shows, so full mixed or series-only collections receive the first 2,000 mapped items in source order.

```sh
./ether plugin check sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin test sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin pack -o ./english-dubs.etherpkg sdk/examples/english-dubs
./ether plugin check ./english-dubs.etherpkg
node --test sdk/examples/english-dubs/tests/plugin.test.ts
```

# Local folders

This hosted source scans the folders you grant to the plugin, matches movies and shows against Ether's catalogue, and returns local files as direct releases. Movie folders use `Title (Year)`; shows use `Show/Season 1/S01E02` filenames. Files remain in their original folders.

## Setup

Run `go run ./cmd/ether plugin check sdk/examples/local-folders` and `go run ./cmd/ether plugin pack -o /tmp/local-folders.etherpkg sdk/examples/local-folders`. Install the package in Server > Plugins and pick the folders to grant to the plugin. Open the Local folders plugin page and choose Scan folders. Use the title picker on unmatched folders to assign a catalogue title. The scheduled scan repeats hourly. Run offline tests with `node --test sdk/examples/local-folders/tests/plugin.test.ts` and `go test ./sdk/examples`.

Screenshot placeholder: the Local folders page with a scan button and an unmatched folder card containing a title search picker. A second screenshot shows the folder grants in the plugin drawer.

## Limits

Only files under the granted roots are indexed. The scanner recognizes MKV, MP4, M4V, AVI, MOV, TS and WebM, and series episodes named with `S01E02`. A folder whose name carries a provider ID tag, as Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyfin and Plex write them (`{tmdb-603}`, `[tmdbid-603]`, `{tvdb-81189}`, `[imdbid-tt0133093]`), is matched by that ID. Otherwise automatic matching requires the catalogue title, compared by letters and digits only (so `Mr. Robot` matches a folder named `Mr Robot` or `Mr.Robot`), and, when present, the year. The scanner follows the folder API cursor to read directories larger than one page. Scans are subject to Ether’s host-call and time budgets; very large trees can exceed them. Scans stop at ten directory levels. Changes are reflected after the next scan, and removing a manual match currently requires removing the plugin's stored data. Ether's existing player support determines which files can be played.

# Sports (`org.ether.sports`)

A first-party hosted TypeScript plugin for Ether that brings live scores, standings, schedules, win probability, play-by-play, and team favourites across 17 leagues using ESPN's public JSON endpoints behind a swappable `SportsProvider` interface.

## What it contributes

- **Live feed (`sports`):** `live_events` capability with a 15 s minimum interval and `team` entity kind. The plugin never polls on its own; Ether calls it on demand while a client is subscribed or an alert window is open.
- **Sports screen (`sports`):** `leagues`, `hero`, `Live now`, `Your teams`, `Today`, `Schedule`, `Standings`, and `Teams` sections matching Ether's generic screen contract and binding Vela wire shapes.
- **Live TV matching:** `broadcasts` (normalized TV / stream / radio with region preference) and `matchHints` (team names, short names, nicknames, locations, abbreviations, and expanded broadcast callsigns) for Ether's "Where to watch" and score-bug overlay matcher.
- **Close-game alerts (`status.close`):**
  - Football (NFL, NCAAF): within 8 points in Q4 under 5 min (or OT within 8).
  - Basketball (NBA, WNBA, NCAAM): within 5 points in the last 3 min of regulation (Q4 for 4-quarter leagues, 2nd half for NCAAM) or OT.
  - Hockey (NHL): tied or within 1 goal in the 3rd period (or OT/SO).
  - Soccer (MLS, EPL, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, UCL): level at or after 80' (or level in extra time).
  - Baseball (MLB): within 2 runs in the 9th inning or extra innings.

## Default leagues

Enabled by default and selectable in plugin settings (`leagues`):

NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB, MLS, Premier League (`epl`), La Liga (`laliga`), Bundesliga (`bundesliga`), Serie A (`seriea`), Ligue 1 (`ligue1`), Champions League (`ucl`), NCAAF top 25 (`ncaaf`), NCAAM top 25 (`ncaam`), WNBA, Formula 1 (`f1`), UFC, and PGA Tour (`pga`).

## Settings and permissions

- **Settings (`settings.schema.json`):**
  - `leagues` (`multiSelect`): leagues included on the Sports screen and live score feed.
  - `region` (`select`): preferred broadcast region (`us`, `ca`, `gb`, `eu`, `au`, or `all`). When an event has no broadcasts for the chosen region, all listed broadcasts are returned as fallback so Live TV matching keeps working.
- **Network permissions:** `site.api.espn.com` and `site.web.api.espn.com` for data, and `a.espncdn.com` for team and league logos. Ether fetches logos itself through its signed image proxy and only from hosts listed here, so clients never load ESPN URLs.

## Plugin endpoints

- `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/events?from=&to=&league=&ids=`
- `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/events/{id}`
- `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/entities?kind=team&league=&q=`
- `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/standings?league=`
- `GET /ether/health`
- `POST /ether/configure`
- `POST /ether/test`

## Architecture and caching

- **Provider interface (`src/providers/types.ts`):** `EspnSportsProvider` (`src/providers/espn.ts`) implements `SportsProvider`. Another provider can be passed to `createSportsHandler({ provider })` without changing routing, settings validation, close-game heuristics, or caching helpers.
- **Concurrency & caching:** outbound requests use `ether.http.fetchMany` capped at 6 concurrent requests per host (chunked at 64 per call). KV cache TTLs are 15 s for scoreboards/details with live (`in`/`delayed`) events, 5 min for non-live scoreboards/details, 15 min for standings, and 24 h for teams/entities. Transient upstream errors fall back to stale cached values when available.
- **Self-contained hosted sources:** all imports stay relative inside `sdk/examples/sports/src/` so Ether Studio can import and edit `src/plugin.ts` directly without external package imports. `src/contract.ts` mirrors the v0.3.19 `live_events` and `screens` contract types locally until they are exported from `@ether/plugin-sdk`.

## Ether Studio recipe

Follow this recipe to open, inspect, customize, and install `org.ether.sports` inside **Ether Studio** (`Server → Plugins → Develop`):

1. **Import or scaffold the draft:**
   - Pack and install `sdk/examples/sports`, then click **Edit in Studio** on `Sports` (all imports stay inside `src/`, so Studio keeps `src/plugin.ts` and sibling modules editable).
   - Or start a hosted TypeScript draft in Studio and copy `manifest.json`, `settings.schema.json`, `assets/icon.svg`, `i18n/en.json`, `i18n/fr.json`, and `src/**`.
   - Confirm `ether.permissions.network` lists only `["site.api.espn.com", "site.web.api.espn.com", "a.espncdn.com"]`.
2. **Exercise routes in the Inspector** (enable live network in the sandbox permissions drawer to hit ESPN):
   - `GET /ether/health` → `{ status: "ok", provider: "espn", feed: "sports", leagues: [...], region: "us" }`.
   - `POST /ether/test` → probes the first enabled league on ESPN and returns `{ ok: true, message }`.
   - `POST /ether/configure` with `{"leagues":["nfl","nba","epl","f1"],"region":"ca"}` → `200`; `{"leagues":[]}` → `400` with `fields["/leagues"]`.
   - `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/events?league=nfl` → `{ events, nextPollSec }` with normalized RFC3339 timestamps, `broadcasts`, and `matchHints`.
   - `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/events/{id}` (for example `nfl-401873066`) → `LiveEventDetail` with `tables`, `plays`, and `probabilitySeries` (`t` as `0..1` game fraction).
   - `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/entities?kind=team&league=nfl&q=eagles` → `{ entities: [{ id: "nfl-21", kind: "team", ... }] }`.
   - `GET /ether/v1/live/sports/standings?league=nba` → sorted conference tables (`#` ascending from `1`).
3. **Customize in Studio:**
   - **Default leagues:** edit `settings.schema.json` `leagues.default` to pre-select a smaller set (for example `["nfl", "nhl", "epl", "f1"]`).
   - **Close-game thresholds:** edit `src/close.ts` (`isCloseGame`) to tune margins or clock thresholds.
   - **Swap data provider:** implement `SportsProvider` (`src/providers/types.ts`), add its host to `ether.permissions.network`, and pass `{ provider }` into `createSportsHandler` in `src/plugin.ts`.
4. **Install and publish:** click **Install** in Studio, review the two ESPN network grants and 64 MiB hosted memory cap, select leagues and region in the plugin drawer, run **Test connection**, and publish the plugin to Vela so the **Sports** screen appears in navigation.

## Limits and ESPN API notes

- Uses ESPN's public, undocumented JSON endpoints (`site.api.espn.com` and `site.web.api.espn.com`), which may change without notice.
- ESPN's team-sport scoreboard endpoints reject `YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD` date ranges with HTTP 400; multi-day windows fan out bounded single-day requests (up to 7 days) through `http.fetchMany`, while multi-day weekend events (`f1`, `pga`, `ufc`) use range queries.
- ESPN returns HTTP 404 for `/summary` on `f1`, `pga`, and `ufc`; event detail falls back to scoreboard data to build race results/weekend sessions, golf leaderboards, and fight cards.
- NBA and MLB standings returned by ESPN are not pre-sorted by rank; the provider sorts entries by `playoffSeed`/`rank` ascending before rendering tables.
- Test fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` are trimmed recordings of real ESPN responses captured on 2026-11-22.

# `etherplugin` (Go SDK)

Go authoring package (`github.com/braedonsaunders/ether/sdk/go`) for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Execution modes

1. **Native HTTP or WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`ether.runtime.kind: "remote"`)**:
   Compile a standard Go binary and call `p.Serve(ctx, etherplugin.ServeOptions{})` (or mount `p` as an `http.Handler`). Host calls go over HTTP to `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`.
2. **Hosted WebAssembly guest**: not yet supported. Go 1.27.3 `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm` emits `wasi_snapshot_preview1` imports (including `proc_exit`, `clock_time_get`, and `fd_write`), which the runtime forbids. TinyGo is not installed here, so a compatible TinyGo build has not been verified. Use a sidecar until a guest is built and tested against Ether's raw WASM ABI.

## Usage

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	etherplugin "github.com/braedonsaunders/ether/sdk/go"
)

func main() {
	p := etherplugin.New(etherplugin.Definition{
		Manifest: etherplugin.Manifest{
			ID:      "org.ether.examples.hello",
			Name:    "Hello plugin",
			Version: "0.1.0",
			Ether: &etherplugin.EtherManifestBlock{
				Protocol:     1,
				Kind:         etherplugin.KindExtension,
				Capabilities: []etherplugin.Capability{etherplugin.CapListSource, etherplugin.CapUI},
				Summary:      "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
				Runtime:      etherplugin.RuntimeDecl{Kind: "remote"},
			},
		},
		Routes: etherplugin.Routes{
			Catalog: func(ctx *etherplugin.Context, req etherplugin.CatalogRequest) (etherplugin.CatalogResponse, error) {
				return etherplugin.CatalogResponse{
					Metas: []etherplugin.CatalogItem{{
						ID:          "tt0133093",
						Type:        req.Type,
						Name:        "Hello from " + req.ID,
						ReleaseInfo: "1999",
					}},
				}, nil
			},
		},
	})

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	_ = p.Serve(ctx, etherplugin.ServeOptions{})
}
```

## Flows: events and actions

Declare `CapEvents` with `Contributes.Events.Publish` to emit schema-validated custom events to Ether Flows via `ctx.PublishEvent(key, payload, correlation)` (remote `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish`, rate-limited to 30/min). Declare `CapFlowActions` with `Contributes.FlowActions` and implement `Routes.FlowAction` to handle `POST /ether/v1/flow-actions/{key}` (or a custom declared `/ether/...` route); `FlowActionRequest.IdempotencyKey` carries `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` for safe deduplication and `FlowActionRequest.DryRun` indicates a test/dry run.

## Debrid cache hints

Declare `CapDebridCacheHints` and implement `Routes.DebridCacheHints` to answer `POST /ether/debrid/hints` with the listed torrents a debrid service holds (`DebridCacheHintsResponse.Cached`, info hash to provider kinds). Ether calls it only on a viewer's Play, under a 500 ms deadline; see `docs/plugin-debrid.md`.

## WS8b interoperability test

Once `internal/plugins/remote` is present, run
`go test -tags ws8b ./sdk/examples/hello/go -run TestWS8bSDKInterop`.
It starts Ether's tunnel server and exercises the Go, Python, and TypeScript
hello sidecars. It requires Python 3 and a Node version with TypeScript support
and WebSocket. The Go SDK reconnects automatically after a dropped tunnel.

## Tunnel recovery

`Start(ctx, ServeOptions{Mode: "tunnel", ...})` returns after the initial
credential authentication and hello/welcome handshake; initial failures are
returned to the caller. After that, dropped connections retry serially with
jittered exponential backoff (50–100 ms initially, capped at 5–10 seconds).
Every attempt re-authenticates and repeats the handshake, with a 10-second
connection/handshake timeout. A connection stable for a minute resets backoff.

In-flight calls fail on disconnect and are not replayed. Ether runtimes resolve
the current connection for subsequent calls. `handle.Done` stays open during
recovery; cancelling `ctx` or calling `handle.Close()` stops active I/O and any
retry, closes the socket, and closes `Done`. `Close` is safe to call repeatedly.
Request cancellation stops that handler without closing the shared tunnel.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket. It needs no inbound
port. Use one when the program must reach a local network, a USB device, or an
installed tool that Ether's sandbox cannot.

Set `ETHER_URL` and pair once:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
./my-sidecar
```

The SDK exchanges the code once, saves the credential, and derives the tunnel
URL from `ETHER_URL`. Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin ›
Connect a sidecar; it is valid for 5 minutes and single use. On later restarts
the saved credential is reused, so no new code is needed.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base. The pair URL and the `ws(s)` tunnel
  URL are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else the OS user config directory
  `…/ether-plugins/<plugin id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`) as JSON with the Ether URL it belongs to. If the tunnel rejects a saved
credential, the file is deleted and startup fails with one line instead of
reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM golang:1.27 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN go build -o /out/sidecar ./cmd/sidecar

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static
COPY --from=build /out/sidecar /sidecar
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
ENTRYPOINT ["/sidecar"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "docker": "ghcr.io/you/my-sidecar:1.0.0",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link. With a Docker image
the console shows a ready `docker run` command, mounting `-v ether-<id>:/data`
so the saved credential survives a restart.

// Host provides access to Ether host services (KV, secrets, HTTP, catalog,
// viewers, collections, folders, owner notifications, and logging).
type Host interface {
	KVGet(ctx context.Context, key string) (string, bool, error)
	KVPut(ctx context.Context, key, value string) error
	KVDelete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	KVList(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]string, error)
	SecretGet(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error)
	Fetch(ctx context.Context, req HostFetchRequest) (HostFetchResponse, error)
	CatalogSearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit, offset int) ([]CatalogTitleSummary, error)
	CatalogGet(ctx context.Context, id string) (*CatalogTitleSummary, error)
	ViewerHistory(ctx context.Context, viewerID int64, limit, offset int) ([]ViewerWatchEntry, error)
	// titleID accepts a catalogue movie/episode ID or an owned playable item ref.
	SetWatchState(ctx context.Context, viewerID int64, titleID string, watched bool) error
	UpsertCollection(ctx context.Context, collection map[string]any) error
	FoldersRoots(ctx context.Context) (FolderRoots, error)
	FoldersList(ctx context.Context, root, path string, options ...FolderListOptions) (FolderPage, error)
	FoldersStat(ctx context.Context, root, path string) (FolderEntry, error)
	FoldersHash(ctx context.Context, root, path string, options ...FolderHashOptions) (FolderHash, error)
	FoldersHashStart(ctx context.Context, root, path string, options ...FolderHashOptions) (FolderHashJob, error)
	FoldersFrame(ctx context.Context, root, path string, options FolderFrameOptions) (FolderFrame, error)
	FoldersHashPoll(ctx context.Context, id string) (FolderHashJob, error)
	FoldersHashCancel(ctx context.Context, id string) (FolderHashJob, error)
	NotifyOwner(ctx context.Context, text string) error
	Log(ctx context.Context, level, message string, attrs map[string]any) error
	// Content-kind host services. KindUpsert/KindDelete need a push-mode
	// kind; ResolveSources needs permissions.sources.
	KindUpsert(ctx context.Context, kindKey string, items []KindItem) (accepted int, err error)
	KindDelete(ctx context.Context, kindKey string, externalIDs []string) error
	KindItems(ctx context.Context, kindKey, cursor string, limit int) (KindPage, error)
	ResolveSources(ctx context.Context, q SourceQuery) ([]SourceCandidate, error)
	CachePut(ctx context.Context, libraryKey, name string, data []byte) (blobRef string, err error)
	CacheOpen(ctx context.Context, blobRef string) ([]byte, error)
	// StreamURL mints a short-lived, scoped ticket for one of this plugin's
	// own kind items and returns the Ether stream URL to embed in a
	// frontend adapter response (spec §6.5). viewerID is the viewer the
	// adapter authenticated.
	StreamURL(ctx context.Context, viewerID int64, itemRef string) (string, error)
}

// MarshalJSON preserves ms:0 on search status entries (Status != "") while
// omitting status/results/ms/reason/error on kind:"indexers" entries (Status == "").
func (s IndexerSearchStatus) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	if s.Status == "" {
		type listing struct {
			IndexerID string `json:"indexerId"`
			Indexer   string `json:"indexer"`
			Kind      string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
			MedianMS  *int64 `json:"medianMs,omitempty"`
			LastMS    *int64 `json:"lastMs,omitempty"`
			LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`
		}
		return json.Marshal(listing{
			IndexerID: s.IndexerID,
			Indexer:   s.Indexer,
			Kind:      s.Kind,
			MedianMS:  s.MedianMS,
			LastMS:    s.LastMS,
			LastError: s.LastError,
		})
	}
	type searchStatus struct {
		IndexerID string `json:"indexerId"`
		Indexer   string `json:"indexer"`
		Status    string `json:"status"`
		Results   int    `json:"results,omitempty"`
		MS        int64  `json:"ms"`
		Reason    string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
		Error     string `json:"error,omitempty"`
		Kind      string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
		MedianMS  *int64 `json:"medianMs,omitempty"`
		LastMS    *int64 `json:"lastMs,omitempty"`
		LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`
	}
	return json.Marshal(searchStatus{
		IndexerID: s.IndexerID,
		Indexer:   s.Indexer,
		Status:    s.Status,
		Results:   s.Results,
		MS:        s.MS,
		Reason:    s.Reason,
		Error:     s.Error,
		Kind:      s.Kind,
		MedianMS:  s.MedianMS,
		LastMS:    s.LastMS,
		LastError: s.LastError,
	})
}

// CandidateRef returns the stable ref matchers report for a candidate.
func (c SourceCandidate) CandidateRef() string {
	switch {
	case c.Ref != "":
		return c.Ref
	case c.InfoHash != "":
		return "infohash:" + strings.ToLower(c.InfoHash)
	case c.Magnet != "":
		return "magnet:" + c.Magnet
	case c.TorrentRef != "":
		return "torrentref:" + c.TorrentRef
	case c.NZBRef != "":
		return "nzbref:" + c.NZBRef
	case c.TorrentURL != "":
		return "torrent:" + c.TorrentURL
	case c.NZBURL != "":
		return "nzb:" + c.NZBURL
	case c.PluginRelease != nil:
		return "plugin:" + c.PluginRelease.Plugin + ":" + c.PluginRelease.ID
	default:
		return c.Title
	}
}

func toFloat64(v any) (float64, bool) {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case float64:
		return t, true
	case float32:
		return float64(t), true
	case int:
		return float64(t), true
	case int64:
		return float64(t), true
	case int32:
		return float64(t), true
	case string:
		n, err := strconv.ParseFloat(t, 64)
		return n, err == nil
	default:
		return 0, false
	}
}

# `ether_plugin` (Python SDK)

Single-file, standard-library-only Python 3.9+ SDK for Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

## Features

- Zero external pip dependencies (`http.server`, `urllib.request`, `json`, `socket`, `base64`).
- Same declarative `plugin(manifest=..., routes=...)` router shape as `@ether/plugin-sdk` and `sdk/go`.
- Runs as an HTTP sidecar (`serve(p, mode="http")`) or an outbound WebSocket tunnel sidecar (`serve(p, mode="tunnel")`).
- Supports Ether Flows custom events (`ctx.ether.events.publish(key, payload, correlation)` -> `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish`) and Flow actions (`routes={"flow_action": ...}` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` and `dryRun`).
- Answers debrid cache hints (`routes={"debrid_cache_hints": ...}` for `POST /ether/debrid/hints`, capability `debrid_cache_hints`; see `docs/plugin-debrid.md`).
- Includes `RemoteHostClient` for `/ether/plugin-host/*` authenticated with `X-Ether-Plugin-Credential`, plus `create_test_harness`, `create_mock_host_client`, `fixtures`, and starter capability templates.

## Usage

```python
from ether_plugin import plugin, serve

hello = plugin(
    manifest={
        "id": "org.ether.examples.hello",
        "name": "Hello plugin",
        "version": "0.1.0",
        "description": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
        "types": ["movie"],
        "idPrefixes": ["tt"],
        "catalogs": [{"type": "movie", "id": "hello", "name": "Hello movies"}],
        "resources": ["catalog", "meta"],
        "ether": {
            "protocol": 1,
            "kind": "extension",
            "capabilities": ["list_source", "ui"],
            "summary": "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
            "runtime": {"kind": "remote"},
        },
    },
    routes={
        "catalog": lambda req, ctx: {
            "metas": [
                {
                    "id": "tt0133093",
                    "type": req["type"],
                    "name": f"Hello from {req['id']}",
                    "releaseInfo": "1999",
                }
            ]
        },
    },
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    serve(hello, background=False)
```

Tunnel mode makes one connection and returns when it drops. Use a process
supervisor to restart the sidecar after a disconnection.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket, so it needs no inbound
port. Pair once and the SDK saves the credential:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
python3 plugin.py
```

Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin › Connect a sidecar; it is
valid for 5 minutes and single use. `serve(plugin, mode="tunnel")` resolves the
credential in this order: an explicit credential, then the saved file, then the
pairing code (exchanged once and saved). With none it raises `CredentialError`
with one clear line.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base; the pair and `ws(s)` tunnel URLs
  are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else `~/.config/ether-plugins/<id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`). If the tunnel rejects a saved credential, the file is deleted and
`serve` raises `CredentialError` instead of reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY plugin.py ether_plugin.py manifest.json settings.schema.json ./
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
CMD ["python3", "plugin.py"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "command": "python3 plugin.py",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link.


Content-kind item dictionaries may include `unavailable: {"code": "no_verified_source",
"detail": "No verified source"}`. Ether keeps these items visible with the reason
and refuses resolution until a later upsert omits the field. `pattern: "file"`
with a `path` is reserved for hosted resolvers with `folders: read`; Python
sidecars cannot access host files or call hosted folder operations. Wire types
for folder pages, hash results and frame references are available in
`ether_plugin.py`. See `docs/plugin-kinds.md`.

### Continuing background jobs

A `job` handler receives `{"name": ..., "continuation": ...}`. Return
`{"continueInMs": 0, "continuation": {"next": 41}, "progress": "Platform 41 of 92"}`
to continue. Return `{"done": True}` or `{"failed": "reason"}` to finish; an
absent `continueInMs` also finishes. Store durable checkpoints in KV to recover
on a later owner-started run after restart. Tokens are at most 64 KiB and progress
at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. The drawer supports progress and cancellation.

Ether uses owner-controlled global/per-plugin ceilings under Plugins: default
2 GiB memory (up to wasm32 4 GiB), 12 hours, effectively unlimited background
compute, hosted WASM instance pool (`poolSize`, default 2, default owner
ceiling 4, raisable up to 16; playback resolves keep a reserved lane and
priority), 8 GiB downloads/member expansion, 32 GiB total
expansion and 65,535 ZIP members. Downloads also obey library cache quotas.
Hosted manifests request `ether.runtime.limits` with `memoryBytes`, `deadline`,
`unitBudget`, `poolSize`, `fetchBytes`, `archiveMemberBytes`,
`archiveExpandedBytes` and `archiveMembers`. Install preview
and detail show requested and granted values. Jobs pause during playback/high
host load and use low CPU/IO priority. A 1,000,000-call sanity bound applies;
viewer browse/search/resolve/playback calls retain tight time and compute budgets.
Remote Python processes manage their own CPU/memory. See the TypeScript SDK
README for route classification, policy APIs and complete job behavior.

# `@ether/plugin-sdk` (TypeScript / JavaScript)

Authoring kit for Ether plugins targeting Ether Plugin Protocol v1 (EPP/1).

The same `plugin({ manifest, routes })` definition runs:
- **Hosted** inside Ether's embedded QuickJS + wazero sandbox (`ether.runtime.kind: "hosted"`), bundled into a single artifact with `ether plugin pack`.
- **As a sidecar** on Node or Bun (`ether.runtime.kind: "remote"`), either serving HTTP directly (`serve(p, { mode: "http" })`) or dialing outbound over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket tunnel (`serve(p, { mode: "tunnel" })`).

Hosted plugins and Studio previews have no direct host filesystem, environment,
process or network access. QuickJS `std` and `os` modules are unavailable.
Use the permission-checked `ether` host APIs for services such as HTTP and
folders. Remote sidecars run under their own operating-system permissions and
are not covered by the hosted sandbox.

## Usage

```ts
import { plugin, serve } from "@ether/plugin-sdk";

const hello = plugin({
  manifest: {
    id: "org.ether.examples.hello",
    name: "Hello plugin",
    version: "0.1.0",
    description: "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
    types: ["movie"],
    idPrefixes: ["tt"],
    catalogs: [{ type: "movie", id: "hello", name: "Hello movies" }],
    resources: ["catalog", "meta"],
    ether: {
      protocol: 1,
      kind: "extension",
      capabilities: ["list_source", "ui"],
      summary: "Minimal greeting plugin for Ether.",
      runtime: { kind: "hosted", entry: "plugin.ts" },
    },
  },
  routes: {
    catalog({ type, id }) {
      return {
        metas: [
          {
            id: "tt0133093",
            type,
            name: `Hello from ${id}`,
            releaseInfo: "1999",
          },
        ],
      };
    },
    meta({ type, id }) {
      return {
        meta: {
          id,
          type,
          name: `Title ${id}`,
          releaseInfo: "1999",
          description: "Sample metadata entry.",
        },
      };
    },
  },
});

export const handle = hello.handle;
export const rank_key = hello.rank_key;
export const cond_match = hello.cond_match;
export default hello;

// In a separate Node/Bun entry point: await serve(hello);
```

## Capabilities and routes

- `catalog` (`GET /catalog/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`)
- `meta` (`GET /meta/{type}/{id}.json`)
- `stream` (`GET /stream/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`) and `openStream` (`GET /ether/open/{streamId}[?file=&fileIndex=]`, also `POST /ether/stream/open`)
- `sourceSearch` (`GET /ether/search`, for a `contributes.source.search` declaration) and `releaseFiles` (`GET /ether/files/{id}`)
- `subtitles` (`GET /subtitles/{type}/{id}[/{extra}].json`, requires `X-Ether-Pick` header)
- `markers` (`GET /ether/markers/{type}/{id}.json`)
- `debridCacheHints` (`POST /ether/debrid/hints`, capability `debrid_cache_hints`: which listed torrents a debrid service holds; see `docs/plugin-debrid.md`)
- `channels` (`GET /ether/channels.json`) and `guide` (`GET /ether/guide/{channelId}.json`)
- `notify` (`POST /ether/notify`)
- `event` (`POST /ether/event`) and `ctx.ether.events.publish(key, payload, correlation?)` (`contributes.events.publish`)
- `flowAction` (`POST /ether/v1/flow-actions/{key}` or declared `/ether/...` route, `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key`, `contributes.flowActions`)
- `view` (`GET /ether/view/{page}`) and `action` (`POST /ether/action/{action}`)
- `tool` (`POST /ether/tool/{name}`) and `job` (`POST /ether/job/{name}`)
- `file` (`GET /ether/file/{path...}`)
- `rankKey` and `condMatch` hot-path exports (`rank_key`, `cond_match`)
- `poster_badges` (`ether.contributes.posterBadges` plus `ctx.ether.badges.set`, `clear`, and `usage`)
- `ai.complete` (`ether.permissions.ai: "complete"` for non-viewer routes — actions, jobs, Flow actions, tools, events, sync, schedules; or `"complete+search"` to also opt in to bounded 20 s cached search completions on Stremio catalog search, kinds search, and frontend adapter search routes via `ctx.ether.ai.complete({ messages, schema?, maxTokens?, temperature?, timeoutMs?, searchQuery? })`)

### Poster badges

Plugins that declare `poster_badges` in `ether.capabilities` and up to 4 sets in
`ether.contributes.posterBadges: [{ key, label, description? }]` (`key` matching
`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`) can push short text badges onto movie and show posters,
such as a `"dub languages"` set (`key: "dub_languages"`, `label: "Dub languages"`)
for an anime plugin or an `"editions"` set (`key: "editions"`, `label: "Editions"`):

```ts
await ctx.ether.badges.set("dub_languages", [
  { title: { type: "show", tmdb: 37854 }, labels: ["EN DUB", "JA"] },
]);
await ctx.ether.badges.set("editions", [
  { title: { type: "movie", imdb: "tt0083658" }, labels: ["FINAL CUT"] },
]);
const usage = await ctx.ether.badges.usage(); // { titles, quotaTitles }
```

Each `badges.set` call accepts up to 500 entries; empty `labels` deletes that
title's badges in the set; each title accepts at most 3 labels per set, 1 to 16
characters from `[A-Z0-9 +&'./-]` (lowercase input is uppercased, anything else
is rejected), up to 200,000 titles per plugin. Ether draws the badges from its
local badge store, the owner can switch each set off in poster overlay settings,
and no plugin call happens while rendering.

Tunnel mode currently makes one connection. Use a process supervisor to
restart the sidecar after a disconnection.

## Sidecars

A sidecar is a remote plugin whose program runs on a machine you choose and
dials out to Ether over the `ether-tunnel-v1` WebSocket, so it needs no inbound
port. Pair once and the SDK saves the credential:

```sh
ETHER_URL=https://ether.example.com \
ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data \
ETHER_PAIRING_CODE=PAIR-1234 \
node server.js
```

Create the code in Ether under Plugins › your plugin › Connect a sidecar; it is
valid for 5 minutes and single use. `serve(plugin, { mode: "tunnel" })` resolves
the credential in this order: an explicit credential, then the saved file, then
the pairing code (exchanged once and saved). With none it throws
`CredentialError` with one clear line.

- `ETHER_URL` — the server's `http(s)` base; the pair and `ws(s)` tunnel URLs
  are derived from it.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL` — an explicit credential; always wins.
- `ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR` — where the credential is saved, else `/data` when it
  exists and is writable (a Docker volume), else `~/.config/ether-plugins/<id>/`.
- `ETHER_PAIRING_CODE` — a one-time code.

The credential is saved at `<state dir>/credential` (mode `0600`, directory
`0700`). If the tunnel rejects a saved credential, the file is deleted and
`serve` throws `CredentialError` instead of reconnecting forever.

A Dockerfile that keeps the credential across restarts:

```dockerfile
FROM node:22-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
VOLUME /data
ENV ETHER_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR=/data
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```

Declare how the console runs it with an `ether.sidecar` manifest block:

```json
"ether": {
  "runtime": { "kind": "remote" },
  "sidecar": {
    "docker": "ghcr.io/you/my-sidecar:1.0.0",
    "docs": "https://example.com/my-sidecar"
  }
}
```

`docker` is an image reference; `download` (an https URL) with `command` (a
single line) is the alternative; `docs` adds a setup link.

Searchable settings: a `select` field with `search: true` shows an explicit search
control in the installed plugin's Settings drawer. Ether forwards `q` and
`locale` to `GET /ether/options/{key}` in `request.query` (array values when hosted). Return an array of
`{value, label}` choices. The chosen string is stored verbatim; a JSON string can
carry coordinates and a display name together. Search never saves settings.
Background requests receive the server process locale (`LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`,
then `LANG`) in the `X-Ether-Locale` header when the caller has not supplied one.

### Owner-controlled resources and continuing jobs

`ether.runtime.limits` requests `memoryBytes`, `deadline` (a positive Go duration
such as `12h`), `unitBudget`, `poolSize`, `fetchBytes`, `archiveMemberBytes`,
`archiveExpandedBytes`, `archiveMembers` and `maxItems`. Ether grants each request up to the
owner's global or per-plugin ceiling. Owners can raise or lower ceilings under
Plugins → Settings and in each plugin's drawer. A per-plugin value overrides the
global value, including raising it. Zero inherits; global zero uses the default.
Saving cancels affected jobs and closes runtimes so lowered ceilings apply.

The default memory ceiling is **2 GiB**, adjustable up to wasm32's **4 GiB**;
omitted guest heap requests still use **32 MiB**, allocated only as needed.
The default call/job time ceiling is **12 hours** and background compute is
effectively unlimited (2^60 units per call); owners and manifests may lower it.
The hosted WASM instance pool defaults to **2 instances** and manifests may
request up to the owner ceiling (default **4**, raisable up to **16**, `poolSize`);
with `poolSize >= 3` at least one instance is reserved exclusively for playback
resolves and background jobs hold at most `poolSize - 2`; with `poolSize == 2`
background jobs and frontend adapters share at most one instance so resolves
and health checks retain a free instance. Queued resolves take priority and
start their execution deadline when an instance is acquired.
The default download and expanded-member ceilings are **8 GiB** each, total
archive expansion **32 GiB**, archive members **65,535**, and stored catalogue
items **2,000,000** (`maxItems`, owner-adjustable with no upper bound). Downloads also obey
the media pool budget and any explicit per-library limit.
The host reports requested fields in the manifest and exact grants as
`runtimeLimits` in install preview and detail, displayed side by side, and exposes
the effective limits for the active call at runtime via `ctx.ether.runtime!.limits()` —
including the route-clamped `deadline` and `unitBudget`, `poolSize`, plus
`readBytes = clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)` for sizing `cache.read`,
`archive.open`, and `archive.read` batches without guessing.

Viewer request-path calls derive their unit budget directly from each route's
deadline (`10,000 units/s`): `/stream/*` and `/ether/open*` get 3 s (30,000 units;
20 s / 200,000 units for Stremio add-ons), `/subtitles/*`, `/ether/subtitles/*` and
`/ether/v1/kinds/*/match` or `/live/resolve` get 5 s (50,000 units).
Kind `/resolve` gets 12 s (120,000 units). `/catalog/*`,
`/meta/*`, `/ether/metadata/*`, `/ether/markers*`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/search`,
`/items/*`, `/ether/search` and `/ether/files/*` get 10 s (100,000 units), further shortened only if the owner sets a
lower ceiling. Ranking stays at its existing 2 ms per-candidate and 50 ms
per-batch defaults. Background kind sync and on-demand facet expansion (`/ether/v1/kinds/*/browse`,
`/changes` and `/expand`), administrative setup, actions, tools, events and jobs use the
owner-granted resources; short health/configuration/view/options/test protocol
deadlines protect the host's control plane. Remote plugin processes manage their
own CPU and memory; owner download/archive ceilings also apply to their host
services.

An action or scheduled call returning `{job: "build-catalogue"}` starts a background continuation job.
Return `{continueInMs: 0, continuation: {next: 41}, progress: "Platform 41 of 92"}`
from its handler to continue. The next `JobRequest.continuation` is that opaque
JSON token. Return `{done: true, progress: "Ready"}` to finish, or
`{failed: "reason"}` to stop. A response without `continueInMs` also finishes.
Non-2xx responses, invalid results and call failures stop the job.

Ether allows 0–300,000 ms between calls with a minimum 100 ms pause. Total wall
time uses the owner time ceiling (12 hours by default), with a 1,000,000-call
sanity bound. Each call gets fresh per-call grants. At most two owner, scheduled or facet-expansion jobs and four playback resolver jobs run per
plugin, and the same route cannot overlap. Job threads use OS background CPU/IO
priority on macOS, Linux and Windows. They pause before calls and host-service
operations during playback, Live TV viewing or high CPU/GPU load; pure compute
runs at reduced scheduling priority. Cancellation interrupts in-flight hosted
calls. Work starts only following an owner action, a declared schedule entry, an on-demand viewer slice expansion (`browse.expand`), or a playback resolve.

Tokens are limited to 64 KiB and progress to 1,024 UTF-8 bytes. The drawer shows
progress and a Cancel button. The owner API provides `GET /api/plugins/{id}/jobs`
and `POST /api/plugins/{id}/jobs/cancel` with `{"path":"/ether/job/build-catalogue"}`.
Status includes total-time and attempt caps. Disabling, removing or reloading a
plugin, or stopping Ether, cancels work. The last sixteen route snapshots per
plugin are retained in memory. Store durable checkpoints in KV (`ctx.ether.kv.usage()` reports `{bytes, keys, quotaBytes, quotaKeys}`, including the 256-byte charge per key) to recover on a
later owner-started or scheduled run after restart; Ether does not restart interrupted jobs automatically.

Owner policy is persisted in `plugins.runtimeLimits` and
`plugins.runtimeOverrides[pluginId]`, with the same resource field names as the
manifest. `GET /api/plugins/runtime-limits` returns policy;
`PUT /api/plugins/runtime-limits` takes `{plugin?: string, limits: {...}}`.
Memory cannot exceed 4 GiB, job time has a one-year sanity bound, and member count
has a 1,000,000-entry sanity bound. ZIP, 7z (Copy/LZMA/LZMA2) and RAR 4/5 support bounded member reads. Solid reads restart at the block beginning per call; prefer large sequential chunks. Decoder memory and input/expansion bytes obey runtime grants. The ZIP directory has a 64 MiB allocation
bound; traversal, encryption, special files and 1000:1 expansion checks remain.
